problem_text:
A distribution center must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component over a 9-week planning window.  
The initial stock at the start of the planning interval is 25 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 9 \), the vendor permits the center to issue a procurement request whose size must fall between 14 and 80 units.  
Nevertheless, every procurement request will require a lead time of 1 week before the components become available to fulfill requirements or rebuild stock.  
The requirement for the component in each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 32 units  
* Week 2: requirement 60 units  
* Week 3: requirement 34 units  
* Week 4: requirement 37 units  
* Week 5: requirement 41 units  
* Week 6: requirement 34 units  
* Week 7: requirement 56 units  
* Week 8: requirement 24 units  
* Week 9: requirement 60 units  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning window, component quantities may take fractional values, and the total quantity of physical stock present at any moment must not surpass the storage limit of 64 units.

In week 1, the maximum procurement quantity is restricted to 43 units.  
In week 2, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 23 units.

The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 5 per unit acquired; the storage expense, which amounts to 3 per unit of stock transferred from one week to the next; and the stockout penalty, which amounts to 6 per unit of unfulfilled requirement. Determine the optimal procurement quantity for each week and monitor the ensuing stock and stockout levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
